why: Between te and the e of the mother's name the copy has a hatched 3-shaped sign and then the J (m); the hatched sign is its own sign even though the type (temeykdiye) does not have it.

The sign at line 5 is a plain closed 3; the long stroke under it starts at the hatching and may be the tail of the lost sign rather than its own, and the type leaves the name empty, so neither p nor ẖ is decided.
The copy has a damaged sign (upright with a base stroke, hatched) after soni, where the type has m of mnitowi.
The copy clearly shows n (rising stroke, 3, long tail) after m and the L-plus-loop to sign before wi, matching the type mnptowi.
The copy has three hatched signs whose shapes suggest n i i, while the type prints only dots there, so the copy and the type do not decide.
